### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f88af4c961aa8e63902d12e45ec5b335a07d5d7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `07638bbaf141b2a97166465ac81bfe2dc0e57368` — the merge of head `5eda3731ce58d22da5da6f10b62f7964b95e89d4` into base `3f88af4c961aa8e63902d12e45ec5b335a07d5d7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 07638bbaf141b2a97166465ac81bfe2dc0e57368 && git checkout 07638bbaf141b2a97166465ac81bfe2dc0e57368
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f88af4c961aa8e63902d12e45ec5b335a07d5d7 5eda3731ce58d22da5da6f10b62f7964b95e89d4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f88af4c961aa8e63902d12e45ec5b335a07d5d7 && git merge --no-ff 5eda3731ce58d22da5da6f10b62f7964b95e89d4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f88af4c961aa8e63902d12e45ec5b335a07d5d7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3f88af4c961aa8e63902d12e45ec5b335a07d5d7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：对象上的“汇总”字段如果是把子记录里普通的本币金额加起来（比如工时单把各条工时的成本相加），现在可以声明为本币，页面上会带货币符号显示，不再是一个光秃秃的数字。
- 为什么做：以前这种声明会被校验拒绝，导致汇总金额和旁边的金额格式对不上。
- 出错会怎样：只是多放行一种以前被拒的写法；原来能用的写法都不变，其他货币写法照样被拒。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事。它放宽了元数据的规则，席位会安排一次约定审核，然后由区域落地。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `76fb831b21a0a33437622b3828730967f54a50fc` · 2026-11-19T08:22Z

- **形态** — 18 files, +312/−144:
  - spec: `record-currency-path.ts`, `stack.zod.ts`, `object.zod.ts`, `field.zod.ts`, plus the `api-surface` / `export-origins` / `liveness` ledgers.
  - objectql: `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`.
  - docs: five pages.
  - tests and one changeset.
  Base `24cc61fa`, K=14 (< 15). `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35387`: not governed, under the 3000-line limit. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`; `spec` minor, `objectql` patch. Both levels are right for the kind.
- **Fixes vs card #35045, per seat ruling record 7000258793**:
  - New exported predicate `isTenantCurrencyAmount(def)`: `type === 'currency'` and `currencyMode ?? 'dynamic'` is `'dynamic'`.
  - Case (d) in both doors now reads it in place of `storedHomeAmountSourceOf`: `defineStack` via `stack.zod.ts`, and the engine registry's `followRefusalsOf` at both ends.
  - **Strictly widening, checked**: the object door's own home-candidate test (`refuseDishonestHomeAmount`, `isHomeCandidate`) already requires a `homeAmount.field` to be a `currency` field in `dynamic` mode. So every child field admitted before is admitted now, and nothing that passed is refused.
  - Still refused, unchanged: `record` and `fixed` children, `number`, `formula` and `summary`.
  - The prescription in `recordCurrencyDynamicRollupNotHomeError` now names the child by its type and lists its home-currency amounts. Its record-mode arm keeps `storedHomeAmountSourceOf` to name the home amount to roll up.
  - The `field.zod.ts` describe and the object-door sentence now speak of the admitted set.
  - The liveness row gains a WIDENED entry. Its reader `summaryDeclaresCurrency` is unchanged and already true for any `dynamic` summary, so LIVE holds.
- **Changeset** — read sentence by sentence against the diff; all of these match:
  - the newly admitted declaration and its reason (D4's tenant `localization.currency`);
  - the old refusal text;
  - one predicate for both doors;
  - the unchanged list: no inference without `currencyConfig`, plus the record, fixed, number, formula and summary refusals;
  - the moved wording of the refusal head and prescription;
  - the levels.
  `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` names `skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` eval 20. That path is governed, so it goes to the seat (below).
- **Pins**:
  - `currency-summary-home-rollup.test.ts` admits:
    - sum / min / max / avg over a plain `dynamic` child amount, writable, readonly or computed;
    - over a readonly plain amount beside a record-mode amount with no `homeAmount`;
    - a plain `dynamic` amount whatever a `homeAmount` says of it.
  - It refuses:
    - a `number` child, naming the home-currency amounts;
    - a `summary` child, even a `dynamic` one;
    - a record-mode child without a home amount, prescribing `homeAmount`;
    - a forged `homeAmount` on a `number` or a `fixed` child.
  - CONTROL: a summary declaring nothing has no currency.
  - `record-currency-guards.test.ts` (engine door):
    - registration in either order;
    - a child re-saved out of the admitted set is refused, naming the roll-up, and a run that leaves a refused pair as it was is not refused for it.
- **门禁** — 70 check-runs on this head: 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure.
- **接受的偏差** — none.
- **范围外去向** — the stale eval 20 expected output is on a governed path, so it is routed to seat 5 with this record.
- **L2 owed (routing)** — `Clause-②: yes (widening)` plus non-test `packages/spec/src/**` → a contract review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. Routed to seat 5.
- **落地条款** — not governed. data-2 lands after the seat's L2 record. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `76fb831b21a0a33437622b3828730967f54a50fc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/record-currency-path.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts

Inputs read: card #35045 and all six of its comments (triage, seat ruling record 7000258793, claim 7001536938, both os-dev-reports, claim amendment 7002901285); PR #35387's body, its 18-file list, its three comments and the net diff against `main`; the 70 check-runs on this head (60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed). ADR-0144 D4, D6 and D8 rule 5, `CurrencyConfigSchema`, `summaryDeclaresCurrency` and the service-analytics currency readers were read in the tree, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`defineStack` case (d), accept-set widened: right.** `collectRecordCurrencyPathErrors` now admits a `sum` / `min` / `max` / `avg` summary declaring `dynamic` (or a `currencyConfig` with no mode, `{}` included) over a child field where `isTenantCurrencyAmount` holds: `type: 'currency'` and `currencyMode ?? 'dynamic'` is `dynamic`. That is the ruling's reading (a plain `dynamic` child amount is in the tenant currency by definition) and D8 rule 5 as written ("as every `dynamic` field does").
- **Strictly a widening: right.** The old test, `storedHomeAmountSourceOf(...) !== undefined`, requires `isStoredHomeField`, which is `currency` + `dynamic` + `readonly` + no `expression`. Every field it admitted satisfies the new predicate, so nothing that parsed is refused.
- **Engine registry door, same accept-set at both registration orders: right.** `followRefusalsOf` reads the same predicate at the parent end (child already registered) and at the child end (parent already registered), on the child field as served. The own-key guard precedes both reads.
- **Object door (`refuseUnadmittedSummaryCurrency`), accept-set unchanged: right.** Only its `admitted` sentence and one refusal clause move. It still passes a `dynamic` summary only when it names a child object and field and carries no `defaultCurrency`.
- **Still refused, unchanged: right.** `record` and `fixed` children, `number`, `formula`, another `summary`, any `count`. A summary with no `currencyConfig` still has no currency, so no published default moves (ruling item 3).
- **A forged shape cannot reach the predicate as `dynamic`: right.** `dynamic` with a `currencyField` or a `homeAmount` is refused by `CurrencyConfigSchema` itself (`refuseRecordModeKeyMismatch`), which an extension's fields also parse through. The predicate reads only `type` and `currencyMode`, so the earlier forged-`homeAmount` hardening is no longer load-bearing for admission; it stays in use only to name the home amount in the record-mode prescription.
- **Public surface: one export added, none removed: right.** `isTenantCurrencyAmount` joins `@objectstack/spec/data` (`api-surface/data.json`, `export-origins/data.json`). `storedHomeAmountSourceOf` stays exported.
- **Refusal text changed in three places: right, and not an accept-set change.** The (d) head, its non-currency arm (now names the child's type and lists the child's home-currency amounts) and the object door's admitted list.
- **Measure-follows half: correctly absent.** The diff touches no `packages/services/service-analytics` file. Ruling item 2 puts the derived-measure half on #35046 with no new measure spelling, so nothing of it belongs here.
- **Renderer: no change needed, as the ruling expected.** `summaryDeclaresCurrency` answers true for any `dynamic` summary and resolves the tenant default, a plain number when none is set.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — on the PR body and in the changeset, agreeing with claim amendment 7002901285.

- `Metadata-protocol: added` is right: one newly accepted declaration on an existing key, and no value refused, no requirement tightened, no meaning or default changed.
- `@objectstack/spec: minor` is right for `added` plus a new export.
- `@objectstack/objectql: patch` is acceptable: its door reads the spec predicate and it declares no protocol of its own. Both packages are in the changeset `fixed` group, so they publish at the same version either way. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- Not BREAKING: no ADR-0087 conversion and no migration entry is owed for a widening.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Final os-dev-report 7002971835 carries `open_questions: []`. The two questions of the earlier blocked report are answered: the commit landed, and the `Metadata-protocol` level was settled by amendment 7002901285.
- A2, summary of a summary kept refused: agreed. The ruling names a child amount, a `summary` is not a `currency` field, and admitting it is one more accepted declaration that needs the seat's word. No escalation.
- File surface beyond the first claim (`stack.zod.ts`, `object.zod.ts`, ledgers, two hand-written pages): covered by amendment 7002901285.
- No merge of `origin/main` before opening: the check-runs ran on the merge ref and are green. Accepted.
- Reverse verification in place of the prescribed ablation: accepted; `Test Core` 10/10 is the gate verdict.
- SQL push-down: not engaged. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; both doors read metadata only.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- **`record-currency-path.ts`: holds.** The predicate is the ruling's sentence and nothing more. "Stored" is accurate without a check: a non-`formula` field with an `expression` is computed at write and stored (`FieldSchema.expression`), so a roll-up can read it. Attempt to break it: a `dynamic` field whose `expression` copies a record-mode amount is admitted, and its total is then labelled with the tenant currency. That mislabel already exists on the child field itself, and the total is drawn exactly as its rows are, so the roll-up adds no new dishonesty. The record-mode and `fixed` prescriptions are unchanged and still correct.
- **`stack.zod.ts`: holds.** The (d) branch still `continue`s after judging, so a `dynamic` summary never falls into the `record` arms below it. The docblock cites D4 for the home currency and D8 rule 5 for the home field, both as the ADR reads.
- **`object.zod.ts`: holds.** Text only, and the text states the predicate's set.
- **`field.zod.ts`: holds.** The `currencyConfig` describe and the `CurrencyConfigSchema` JSDoc state the admitted set as the two doors enforce it; the regenerated reference pages carry the same sentence.
- **`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts` (first consumer): agrees with the contract.** Same predicate, same message builder, both orders, judged as served. A child re-saved out of the admitted set is refused naming the roll-up, as before.
- N1 (nit) — The `Skills-docs:` line is real and under-scoped. Eval 20's `expected_output` in `skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` does end "`dynamic` is admitted only on a roll-up of a home amount", and its assertions do not read that sentence. But `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md:179-184` also teaches the roll-up's currency and says `defineStack` "refuses `'dynamic'` on any other roll-up", which this head makes false. The changeset's "no SKILL.md teaches a summary's currency" is true only to the letter. The follow-up card must name both files; the PR body's line can be widened without moving the head.
- N2 (nit) — `record-currency-path.ts` module header still ends "Messages only and two predicates"; it now exports three.
- N3 (nit) — The fallback arm, reached by a `currency` child whose config is neither `dynamic` nor a well-formed `record` or `fixed` (a stored `fixed` row with no code), reads "is a 'currency' field, not a `currency` field in `dynamic` mode". True, but it does not say what is wrong with the field.
- N4 (nit) — Outside the diff, for a follow-up card: `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.summary-dynamic-currency-rollup-home-amount-judged-as-served.ts` still says a `dynamic` summary "is right only for a roll-up of a stored home amount", and its acceptance step "save one over another child field and confirm 422" no longer holds for a plain `dynamic` amount. The comments in `ui/packages/fields/src/currency.ts`, `index.tsx` and `widgets/SummaryField.tsx` are narrow in the same way; behaviour there is right.
